conviction_note: Q3 is new and the trading statement is where this company re-sets its full-year range (Q3 2025 moved to the high end), so abs_move is 5.5 on observed day-after moves of 2.7-6.2% ex the PepsiCo day; the evidence leans slightly negative (Finnish competitor Olvi's weak, cool-weather Q3 and profit warning, a demanding H2 requirement off a +15% Q3 2025 base after a 4.4% Q2 EBIT miss) against a healthy Danish/Nordic category (Carlsberg, DMI) and no nedjustering filed, so p_up 46 and the scaled number (-0.44) sits well under the findings' sum (-1.0) because the lean rests on proxies and inference, not a company number.

already_public.what: H1 2026: Q2 EBIT 753m (consensus 788m per Finwire), Q2 organic volume -0.9%; FY2026 guide reiterated: organic EBIT growth 6-10%, EBIT DKK 2,325-2,425m, net revenue broadly flat
PepsiCo licences in DK/FI/Baltics (~13% of net revenue) end at end-2028; EBIT growth in line with 6-8% target to end-2028 (stock -24.8% that day)
New buyback of up to DKK 300m running to Dec 2026 (previous programme 700m); weekly buyback reports through 2026-11-09, no inside-information or guidance announcement since 2026-04-21

new_in_release.expect: Q3 volume/revenue/EBIT, first look at July-Sept; base is Q3 2025 EBIT 777m (+15%) with a 'strong Q3 in Finland'. Expect EBIT roughly flat to low-single-digit up: Finland soft (Olvi), Denmark healthy (Carlsberg, DMI), cost inflation. Slight negative vs an unsourced bar.

Most likely: range kept or narrowed. H2 needs EBIT 1,299-1,399m vs 1,243m in H2 2025 (+4.5% to +12.5%); narrowing toward the low/middle is the more likely direction than to the high end. A cut below 2,325m is unlikely because no nedjustering has been filed six weeks after quarter-end.
Q4 commentary on cost inflation (energy, packaging, freight) and on 2027 framing; unknown direction.
Q3 free cash flow; unknown. Net debt rose to 6.6bn in H1 per Inderes; buyback cut to 300m.

bar: Full-year bar is the company's own guide, EBIT DKK 2,325-2,425m (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bbd1e9cb6dd93d57c299878f5057fdfff&lang=en&src=listed). No Q3 2026 consensus could be sourced (Finwire/placera, Inderes, company IR page all searched; Royal Unibrew does not publish a consensus page), so the quarterly bar is UNSOURCED and every finding that depends on it is capped small.
session_check: amc -- the issuer's financial calendar lists 'Nov 11, 2026 Trading Statement Q3 2026' with the call on 'Nov 12, 2026, 9 am CET' (https://www.royalunibrew.com/investor/investor-insights/financial-calendar), and the issuer's own scheduled releases land after the 17:00 CET close: Q3 2025 trading statement 2025-11-12 17:06:56 CET, H1 2026 2026-08-17 17:11:43 CEST, Annual Report 2025 2026-02-26 17:28:14 CET (Nasdaq Nordic feed, https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b9f22bdca06b01da7a5b8aeae12481058&lang=en&src=listed). Only Q1 2026 (10:40) was intraday, and it was pulled forward by the PepsiCo inside-information announcement. So the reaction window is close 2026-11-11 -> close 2026-11-12, not the sealed bmo window.
positioning_check: Finanstilsynet aggregated net short 3.96% (prev 3.75%, +0.21pt, building), as of 30-10-2026 per the baseline (https://www.dfsa.dk/financial-themes/capital-market/company-announcements/aggregated-net-short-positions). Danish register publishes from 0.1%, so not comparable with a 0.5%-threshold aggregate. Moderate and building into the print: the slight negative lean here agrees with it, so the negatives are trimmed. Separately the Chair bought 2,000 shares at DKK 434.86 on 2026-08-18 (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b4cc2e1bca9145256b70534977d5de14f&lang=en&src=listed), small. The +12% 20d run-up is sector beta: Carlsberg +16.8% and Heineken +19.2% over 2026-10-08 -> 11-10 against RBREW +13% (Yahoo daily closes), so the run-up does not price anything company-specific.

findings.finding: Olvi, Royal Unibrew's main Finnish competitor, reported Q3 2026 Finland volume -4.4% on a cool late summer and weak demand, cut its FY2026 profit guide on 13 Oct (tulosvaroitus) and cited Iran-war cost inflation on freight and packaging; Finland is one of Royal Unibrew's two largest markets and its Q3 2025 comp was 'strong Q3 performance in our key Finnish market'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2025 (cold Finnish weather, soft Q2) and H1 2026 (Q2 volume -0.9%, EBIT 4.4% below consensus) both sold: -2.31% on the H1 2025 day and -5.17% on 2026-08-18; Q3 2025, with Finland strong, rose +4.02%.
findings.original_quote: Loppukesän viileä sää ei tukenut kuluttajakysyntää erityisesti Suomessa, mikä näkyi varsinkin vesien myynnissä ja heikensi volyymia kolmannella neljänneksellä. (The cool weather in late summer did not support consumer demand, especially in Finland, which was particularly reflected in water sales and weakened volume in the third quarter.) English version, same day: 'The third-quarter volume decreased by 4.4%' (https://mb.cision.com/Main/14712/4413640/4331929.pdf).
findings.why_not_priced: Olvi published 22 Oct and RBREW then rose with the beer sector (+13% in 20 days vs Carlsberg +17%, Heineken +19%), so the market has treated RBREW as a sector-beta name, not marked down Finland. If this were priced, RBREW would have lagged peers by more than the ~4-6 points it has, or the Danish register would show a sharper build than +0.21pt. Partly priced: the lag versus peers may already reflect it, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Royal Unibrew's own Q3 2025 statement sets the tough Finnish comp ('Strong Q3 performance in our key Finnish market, following a soft Q2 due to cold weather', https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b9f22bdca06b01da7a5b8aeae12481058&lang=en&src=listed); no independent Q3 2026 Finnish market statistic (Panimoliitto) was found.

findings.finding: The Danish and wider Nordic category was healthy in Q3 2026: Carlsberg reported Nordic volumes 'grew solidly' in Q3, led by soft drinks, premium beer and alcohol-free beer, and DMI records July 2026 as dry and very sunny against a very wet July 2025, with summer 2026 the eighth-warmest since 1874. Denmark is Royal Unibrew's largest market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When the Northern Europe weather and volume line helped (Q3 2025), the stock rose +4.02% the next day; H1 2026 says Q2 2026 volumes 'benefited from more favorable weather' and the stock still fell 5.17% on the margin miss.
findings.original_quote: DMI, Sammendrag af juli 2026: 'Tør, meget solrig og lidt varm.' (Dry, very sunny and slightly warm.) vs Sammendrag af juli 2025: 'Tiendevådeste siden 1874, meget varm og med lidt under gennemsnitlig solskin.' (Tenth-wettest since 1874, very warm and slightly below-average sunshine.) https://www.dmi.dk/fileadmin/user_upload/Afrapportering/Maanedssammendrag/Sammendrag_2026_juli.pdf ; https://www.dmi.dk/fileadmin/user_upload/Afrapportering/Seasonsammendrag/Sammendrag_2026_sommer.pdf ('Ottendevarmeste siden 1874, tør og meget solrig').
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Carlsberg rose sharply after its 29 Oct statement and RBREW followed. What would look different if it were fully priced is RBREW keeping pace with Carlsberg; it lagged by about 4 points. It could also mean Carlsberg took share from RBREW in Denmark, which is why the range reaches below zero.
findings.independence: DMI monthly and summer summaries (https://www.dmi.dk/fileadmin/user_upload/Afrapportering/Maanedssammendrag/Sammendrag_2026_august.pdf: August 'Solrig, under normal nedbør og normal temperatur') are an independent series that points the same way for Denmark.

findings.finding: The reiterated guide asks a lot of H2: EBIT of DKK 2,325-2,425m on H1 EBIT of 1,026m needs H2 EBIT of 1,299-1,399m against 1,243m in H2 2025 (+4.5% to +12.5%), on a Q3 2025 base of 777m that grew 15%, after a Q2 EBIT miss of 4.4% and stated 'increasing inflationary pressure across several cost categories'. Narrowing the range toward the low or middle end at this trading statement is more likely than a move to the high end. A cut below the range is unlikely: no nedjustering (inside-information announcement) has been filed since 21 April, six weeks after Q3 closed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 statement narrowed the guide to 'the high end of the 8-12% range' and the stock rose +4.02% the next day; the FY2025 release, with the 2026 first guide, fell -2.35%; H1 2026, guide reiterated with a miss, fell -5.17%.
findings.why_not_priced: The H2 arithmetic is public but the price has followed the sector (+13% in 20 days) rather than the guide-risk. If a low-end narrowing were priced, RBREW would not have rallied with Carlsberg and Heineken, and Q3 previews would carry a lower-end FY EBIT. Sized small because the no-warning fact bounds the downside, the quarterly bar is unsourced, and shorts are already building.
findings.independence: Finwire's H1 table (Q2 EBIT 753 vs consensus 788, https://www.placera.se/telegram/royal-unibrew-royal-unibrews-rorelseresultat-samre-an-vantat-20260817) and Olvi's 13 Oct guidance cut on cost pressure (https://mb.cision.com/Main/14712/4413640/4331929.pdf) point the same way. Nasdaq Nordic feed shows no Royal Unibrew inside-information release after 2026-04-21, which points the other way on a cut below the range.

outside_window.finding: PepsiCo licence exit at end-2028 (~13% of net revenue); 2029 earnings impact quantified only later

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly negative while priced_lean is +1.34 (short squeeze component) and the 20d run-up is +12%. The run-up is sector beta (RBREW lagged Carlsberg and Heineken), and the negatives agree with a building short, so they are trimmed and p_up sits only 4 points below 50.
language_note: The filings added nothing: Royal Unibrew publishes only in English on the Nasdaq Nordic feed, and so do Carlsberg and Olvi (Olvi files Finnish and English versions with identical content).
DMI's Danish-language monthly and summer summaries gave the Danish Q3 weather comparison (sunny, dry July 2026 vs a tenth-wettest July 2025). No English source carried it.
Swedish Finwire copy on placera.se carried the company-compiled Q2 consensus table (EBIT 788m expected vs 753m actual) that the English wire summaries left out.
Danish-language searches for a Q3 preview, analyst actions and retail sentiment returned nothing the English sources did not already carry.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide': this trading statement is where the company re-set its range a year ago, so a guidance change is plausible. abs_move_pct went from 5.0 to 5.5.
'Positioning is the thing to beat': the two negative findings agree with a building short (+0.21pt), so the Olvi finding went from -0.8 to -0.7 and p_up from 45 to 46.
'Too small about the move': I kept the guidance finding at -0.9 and widened its range to -3.5 / +1.5 instead of shrinking it.
'Session is load-bearing': opened session_check with amc and the issuer's own timestamps.
